comments.body: Moved to its own project on 2026-10-17: ~/src/quartermaster (command qm). The owner chose a separate tool that Muster shows, rather than a Muster feature, because projects' ./dev scripts, beagle jobs and the owner at a plain shell need it whether or not Muster is running. Its docs/origin.md answers this card's questions: it arbitrates (a queue against a per-machine budget) and also informs; priority comes from the owner's standing ranking and his notes of the moment; machines and the usage limit are two mechanisms behind one place to ask. Muster's likely part: attributing processes to panes through MUSTER_PANE, a queued job's reason in the pane's waiting state, and messages to lead agents who subscribe. Quartermaster's card 'The agent interface: qm docs, a skill, hooks for Claude Code and Codex, and Muster' tracks that.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Agents from different projects share one Mac and one account's weekly usage limit, and each project works out its share alone. Today that is ad hoc: caps written into each project's CLAUDE.md, a lock script per repo, and messages between orchestrators. Needs its own design pass, probably a MIP, before anything is built.

Sightings:

- 2026-10-16 night: muster's integrator and spool's integrator took turns at full gates by `muster msg` ("gate starting", "gate done"). Each wait cost a turn, and a post was refused while the other side had unread messages. Gates run side by side flaked under load: a_2hLJLXgsA failed four gates that night and passes alone.
- A private project that runs up to ten Muster workers: its CLAUDE.md caps it at about four concurrent agents because other projects share the 16 GB Mac. A card on its board copies spool's `tools/gate-lock`, an fcntl lock. On 2026-10-13 its orchestrator asked spool's and chat-notes' orchestrators by message to warn it before heavy work, so it could hold off a long export job.
- Disk: that project stops below 10 GB free, and muster's integrator freed 3.1 GB with `cargo clean` at 12 GB free on 2026-10-16.
- Usage: its orchestrator checks the account's weekly limit before every dispatch and stops at 25% left. Every project's agents draw on that budget, and none sees the others' spending.
- `./dev --perf` refuses to run on a loaded machine, and cannot say whose load it is (`./dev --doctor` lists processes, not agents).

Questions for the design:

- Which resources count: CPU, memory, disk, the account's usage limit, and things only one job may hold at a time (the logged-in GUI session `--contract` needs, a devenv container).
- Does Muster arbitrate (hold locks and queues) or only inform (show which agent runs which heavy job, and let agents agree)? A queued agent could read `waiting` with the reason, rather than `working`.
- Priority between projects is the person's call. How do they state it, so that agents do not guess? a_2YSLgtM5f carries the same warning about agents coordinating on their own.
- CPU and memory are per machine, the usage limit is per account: one design or two?
- Is Muster the home for this at all, given that it imposes no workflow, or is it a separate tool that Muster shows?

Related: a_2die8Xhxs (usage telemetry), a_2YSLgtM5f.
title: Machine sharing: agents from several projects contend for one machine and one usage limit
